(1) Budget corners: buildBuddyGraph(1000,12)=44.2s at exactly MAX_GREEDY_WORK, (5000,2)=2.3s, (3000,2)=1.1s; buildConstrainedBuddyGraph (5000,0)=1.5s, (5000,1)=3.2s, (5000,2)=4.7s, (5000,4)=17.0s, (464,463)=54.3s — all inside the documented envelopes. (2) Tried to outrun constrainedWork via many-component inputs that force repairConnectivity/swapJoin's unbudgeted O(components^2) outer scan to repeat over many passes: hub-star with 499 prohibited groups at n=1500 (1.12M pairs, est 9.4e7) ran 3.3s; required-triangle saturation at n=4998 (1666 components) ran 1.8s (all edges required, so swapJoin skips them). saturationDecisions.why: at gate (4) but a changed path is on its surface

themes.theme: Non-finite numbers break formatReason's byte-for-byte parity with the Python oracle
findingSummaries: formatReason interpolates raw numbers, so NaN/Infinity render as "NaN"/"Infinity" where reference-python's format_reason renders "nan"/"inf", breaking the docblock's byte-identical contract on the exact inputs Reason.person is documented to carry; the same raw interpolation recurs in constrainedGreedy.ts's checkWellFormed/checkConstraintIds throw messages.
themes.remediation: Add a single num(x) formatting helper in constraints.ts (mapping NaN->"nan", Infinity->"inf", -Infinity->"-inf", else stringify) and route every number interpolation in formatReason and in constrainedGreedy.ts's throw messages through it, removing the ad hoc raw interpolations at each call site.

themes.theme: Graph's public index-taking read methods apply the vertex guard inconsistently
findingSummaries: Graph.degree/degrees are public read paths with no #checkEndpoints call, so degree(-1) throws a raw unnamed TypeError while degree("0") silently returns a real answer, contradicting the in-file rationale that the read path is guarded to avoid reporting a phantom edge for a non-vertex.
themes.remediation: Call the existing #checkEndpoints (or a one-argument #checkVertex extracted from it) at the top of degree(), removing the special-cased unguarded entry point rather than adding a new check elsewhere; degrees() needs no change since it takes no index.

themes.theme: constraints.ts entry points perform unbounded or ungated work before the module's own refusal gate can run
findingSummaries: validateDetailed's structural-error path is unbounded in work and output: structuralReasons pushes unlimited Reason objects, normalize builds/sorts an unbounded Map, and the full pair scan plus normalize run before the O(1) n>MAX_CONSTRAINED_N and constrainedWork refusals that could have decided alone, violating the module's own 'refuse before any n-sized allocation would overflow' comment.

Constraints.fromTags takes n on faith with no Number.isInteger/range guard (unlike degreeOf, the Graph constructor, and validate in the same file) and runs an O(n^2) double loop materializing prohibited pairs inside the constructor before validate's MAX_CONSTRAINED_N refusal can ever run; currently unreachable from any caller outside lib/test, so filed as a deferral, but shares the identical root cause of gates not being enforced ahead of unbounded work.
themes.remediation: Enforce one rule at every constraints.ts entry point: cheap O(1)/O(n) guards run and can refuse before any O(n^2) or O(P) work begins, and no code path accumulates more than a fixed, bounded amount of output. Concretely: hoist the n>MAX_CONSTRAINED_N/constrainedWork checks in validateDetailed ahead of the pair scan, cap structuralReasons to a small fixed count (collapsing overflow into one summarising reason) so normalize's Map/sort stays O(1) in P, and add the same Number.isInteger/range guard fromTags is missing (mirroring degreeOf) before its double loop, pre-counting group sizes to refuse via the existing pair cap instead of building the O(n^2) set. This removes the duplicate, inconsistently-placed guards rather than introducing a new gating abstraction.

themes.theme: PROJECT_PLAN.md's architecture snapshot describes a rejected design
findingSummaries: docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md still describes a two-tier (label-assignment default / core-aware fallback) constraint design that docs/findings/CONSTRAINT_FINDINGS.md rejected before M1 shipped; lib/src implements only the single validated core-aware tier, with no anonymous-graph-then-seat path anywhere in the code.
themes.remediation: Delete/replace the superseded two-tier description in PROJECT_PLAN.md section 3 with a pointer to CONSTRAINT_FINDINGS.md's conclusion, removing the stale text rather than layering a correction alongside it.

themes.theme: buildReport parameter name names only one of the two code paths it covers
findingSummaries: Parameter `priorsWeighed` in buildReport actually means 'priors were accounted for by either promotion or soft weighting', but the name mentions only weighing, misleading a reader who traces just the buildReport function.
themes.remediation: Rename `priorsWeighed` to `priorsAccountedFor` (or `priorsConsidered`) and update the call-site comment at lines 434-438 to match, removing the narrower name rather than adding clarifying comments alongside it.

gating.theme: validate's refusal prose is contractually pinned byte-for-byte to the Python oracle, but non-finite numbers render differently in the two runtimes, so the parity claim silently fails on exactly the values the Reason type says can arrive
gating.summary: formatReason interpolates raw numbers, so NaN/Infinity render as "NaN"/"Infinity" where reference-python's format_reason renders "nan"/"inf" — breaking the docblock's "byte-identical to the Python reference's" contract on the very inputs `Reason.person` is documented to carry.
gating.failure: validate(new Constraints(4), NaN) -> ["buddy count NaN must be a non-negative whole number"]; Python validate(Constraints(4), float('nan')) -> ["buddy count nan must be a non-negative whole number"]. Same divergence for validate(new Constraints(Infinity), 4) ("roster size Infinity" vs "roster size inf"), new Constraints(NaN) ("NaN" vs "nan"), and c.prohibit(Infinity, 1) ("unknown person Infinity" vs "unknown person inf"). Reproduced side by side over a 3,000-case fuzz of (n, k, prohibited, required, priors): 2,993 messages matched byte-for-byte, all 7 mismatches were this one class. The existing suite (reasons.test.ts, constrained.test.ts message tests) only uses finite values, so it passes.
gating.remediation: Normalise at the single formatting boundary rather than at each call site: add one `num(x)` helper in constraints.ts that maps NaN->"nan", Infinity->"inf", -Infinity->"-inf" and otherwise stringifies, and route every interpolation in formatReason through it. Mirror the same rendering in reference-python only if the reverse direction is preferred; either way, pick one and pin it. The sibling to close in the same edit: the identical raw-number interpolation in constrainedGreedy.ts's checkWellFormed/checkConstraintIds throw messages, which mirror the same reasons.
gating.invariant: For every Reason r reachable from validateDetailed (including ones carrying NaN/±Infinity in `n`, `k`, `person`, `a`, `b`), formatReason(r) is byte-identical to reference-python's format_reason of the same reason — checkable by extending the reference fixture with non-finite cases and asserting equality, rather than by listing which values to try.

gating.theme: Graph's vertex-index guard is applied to some public read methods and not their siblings, so an out-of-range index gets a clear named error on one method and a bare TypeError (or a silently wrong answer) on the next
gating.summary: Graph.degree/degrees are public read paths with no #checkEndpoints call, so degree(-1) throws a raw TypeError naming nothing, while degree("0") returns a real answer — directly contradicting the in-file rationale that the read path is guarded so it "cannot report a phantom edge for a non-vertex".
gating.failure: const g = new Graph(3); g.addEdge(0,1). g.hasEdge(-1,0) -> Error: "vertex -1 must be an integer in [0, 2]" (good). g.degree(-1) -> TypeError: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'size')" — no index named. Same for 3, 1.5 and null. Worse, g.degree("0") returns 1: adj["0"] aliases adj[0], so a non-number index that hasEdge refuses is silently accepted here. metrics.ts already added checkVertex to bfsDistances for exactly this reason ("a bad index produced TypeError: g.adj[u] is not iterable instead of the module's own message"); degree/degrees is the sibling that was left open. Nothing in the suite covers it — optimizer.props.test.ts:641 pins only bfsDistances.
gating.remediation: Call the existing #checkEndpoints (or a one-argument #checkVertex extracted from it) at the top of degree(). degrees() needs nothing — it takes no index. This is subtraction of a special case, not new machinery: every public index-taking entry point then answers the same way. Verify the internal hot-loop callers (legalEdge, deficientVertices, choosePartner, findPair, repairDegrees) still pass validated indices so the added check is O(1) and never fires.
gating.invariant: Every exported entry point that takes a vertex index (Graph.addEdge/removeEdge/hasEdge/degree, metrics' bfsDistances/shortestPath/eccentricity) throws an Error whose message contains the offending value, for every argument that is not an integer in [0, n-1] — no TypeError, and no value returned.

gating.theme: the refusal path's cost and output grow without bound with the size of the caller's constraint set, so the cheap gate becomes the expensive step
gating.summary: validateDetailed's structural-error path is unbounded in both work and output size. structuralReasons (line 331) pushes up to two Reason objects per malformed pair with no cap; normalize (line 223) then calls formatReason on every one, builds a Map of up to 2P entries and sorts 2P strings (O(P log P) with string comparison); validate (line 322) maps formatReason over the survivors a second time. The module's own comment at line 338 states the contract this breaks: 'Refuse before any n-sized allocation would overflow — validate must not throw.' Aggravating: for any n <= MAX_ROSTER the full pair scan and normalize run BEFORE the O(1) n > MAX_CONSTRAINED_N and constrainedWork refusals, so the gate that could have decided alone runs after the work. NOT reachable from BuddyGraph today: app/src/constraints.ts:34 caps at MAX_CONSTRAINT_PAIRS = 200 and app/src/io/importGraph.ts:189 refuses a file above it — hence suggestion, not blocking. It matters because lib/ ships as a standalone zero-dependency package whose documented entry contract is that validate refuses rather than throws, and because validateDetailed has a live MAIN-THREAD caller (app/src/panels/RosterModal.tsx:145) that renders whatever array it returns.
gating.failure: new Constraints(10) with 1,000,000 prohibited pairs whose endpoints are all >= 10 (c.prohibit(1000+2i, 1001+2i)): validateDetailed(c,4) returns 2,000,000 Reason objects, taking 5.0 s and growing RSS from 197 MB to 925 MB; validate(c,4) then spends a further 7.9 s producing 2,000,000 strings — on a ten-person roster. Scaling up: new Constraints(1_000_000) with 2,000,000 such pairs takes 35.5 s and 1.6 GB inside validate and returns 4,000,000 strings, even though cons.n exceeds MAX_CONSTRAINED_N and would be refused in O(1) if that cap ran first; at 4,000,000 pairs (caller's own Set fits in a 2 GB heap at ~600 MB) node dies with a V8 FatalProcessOutOfMemory inside validate — i.e. validate throws. Reproducers: .review-scratch/p9.mjs, p10.mjs, p11.mjs.
gating.remediation: Cap the structural error list. Stop accumulating after a small fixed number of distinct structural reasons and emit one summarising variant instead (e.g. { code: "too-many-invalid-constraints", count }), so normalize's Map build and sort are always over a constant-size list and validate's second formatReason map is O(1) in P. The scan itself stays O(P), which is unavoidable and matches the caller's own Set, but the 5x memory amplification, the O(P log P) string sort and the unbounded return array all disappear. Secondarily, hoist the O(1) cons.n > MAX_CONSTRAINED_N and constrainedWork refusals ahead of the pair scan (or run them as an early-out when they alone are decisive) so an input the caps refuse never pays the scan; keep the existing 'most fundamental fault first' ordering for inputs the caps accept.
gating.invariant: For every Constraints value and every k, validateDetailed(cons, k) RETURNS (never throws, never OOMs) and validateDetailed(cons, k).length is bounded by a fixed constant that does not depend on cons.prohibitedCount, cons.priorCount or the number of required pairs — equivalently, the reason count is O(1) in the size of the constraint sets rather than O(P).

gating.theme: Parameter name describes only one code path, not the actual semantic
gating.summary: Parameter `priorsWeighed` in buildReport represents 'priors were accounted for by either promotion or soft weighting', but the name only mentions weighing
gating.failure: New contributor reads `function buildReport(..., priorsWeighed: boolean)` and infers it means 'priors were weighed in polish'. Line 596 uses this to decide whether to compute priorsKeptFraction. But at call site line 439, the fourth argument is `active.priorHard || (priorsWeighed && priorWeight !== 0)`, meaning the boolean can be true because priors were promoted to required edges (active.priorHard), not because they were weighed. The postcondition guarantee (line 699-703, dev-mode only) ensures all required edges are present, so priorsKeptFraction computes correctly to 1.0 in this case, but the parameter name does not reveal this dual-meaning to someone reading buildReport in isolation.
gating.invariant: Whenever buildReport is called, its fourth parameter is true if and only if priors were accounted for by either (1) promotion to required edges via priorHard, or (2) soft weighting in polish with non-zero weight. The parameter name should reflect this disjunction, not only one case.
gating.remediation: Rename parameter from `priorsWeighed` to `priorsAccountedFor` (or `priorsConsidered`). Update the call site comment at line 434-438 to reference the new name. This removes the trap where a maintainer reading only the buildReport function infers the wrong semantic.

confirmed.summary: Constraints.fromTags takes n on faith — no Number.isInteger / range check, unlike degreeOf in the same file (line 35), the Graph constructor and validate — and then runs a double loop materializing one Set key per same-tag pair, so O(n^2) prohibited pairs are built inside the constructor before validate's MAX_CONSTRAINED_N refusal can ever run. ALREADY RECORDED as a tracked follow-on in lib/CLAUDE.md; I re-verified reachability rather than re-deriving the defect. Filed as a deferral only: a grep across app/src, mock and scripts finds no caller of fromTags outside lib/test, so nothing untrusted reaches it in the current tree. It becomes live the moment the tag UI (F6) lands.
confirmed.failure: Traced, not run to completion by design: fromTags(1e15, []) enters `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)` with no guard on n and never exits (the inner loop is skipped because every tag is null, so the hang is the outer loop alone). fromTags(3000, Array(3000).fill('A')) builds ~4.5M Set keys inside the constructor; at tens of millions of pairs the Set construction itself throws before validate sees the input. A NaN tag never groups (NaN !== NaN), silently inverting the documented prohibit_same contract.
confirmed.remediation: When F6 lands: guard n exactly as degreeOf does (Number.isInteger, 0 <= n <= MAX_ROSTER) as the first statement, then pre-count group sizes and refuse against an explicit pair cap — sum over groups of C(size,2) — BEFORE entering the double loop, so the refusal is O(n) and never pays the quadratic materialization. Normalise NaN tags to null in the same pass.
confirmed.invariant: For every n and every tags array, Constraints.fromTags(n, tags) either throws in time O(n) or returns, and it never allocates more than a fixed cap of pair keys — i.e. its running time is bounded by a function of the pairs it is allowed to emit, not by n^2 for an unvalidated n.

deferrals.theme: an attacker-chosen roster size drives unbounded work before any gate can refuse it
deferrals.summary: Constraints.fromTags takes n on faith — no Number.isInteger / range check, unlike degreeOf in the same file (line 35), the Graph constructor and validate — and then runs a double loop materializing one Set key per same-tag pair, so O(n^2) prohibited pairs are built inside the constructor before validate's MAX_CONSTRAINED_N refusal can ever run. ALREADY RECORDED as a tracked follow-on in lib/CLAUDE.md; I re-verified reachability rather than re-deriving the defect. Filed as a deferral only: a grep across app/src, mock and scripts finds no caller of fromTags outside lib/test, so nothing untrusted reaches it in the current tree. It becomes live the moment the tag UI (F6) lands.
deferrals.failure: Traced, not run to completion by design: fromTags(1e15, []) enters `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)` with no guard on n and never exits (the inner loop is skipped because every tag is null, so the hang is the outer loop alone). fromTags(3000, Array(3000).fill('A')) builds ~4.5M Set keys inside the constructor; at tens of millions of pairs the Set construction itself throws before validate sees the input. A NaN tag never groups (NaN !== NaN), silently inverting the documented prohibit_same contract.
deferrals.remediation: When F6 lands: guard n exactly as degreeOf does (Number.isInteger, 0 <= n <= MAX_ROSTER) as the first statement, then pre-count group sizes and refuse against an explicit pair cap — sum over groups of C(size,2) — BEFORE entering the double loop, so the refusal is O(n) and never pays the quadratic materialization. Normalise NaN tags to null in the same pass.
deferrals.invariant: For every n and every tags array, Constraints.fromTags(n, tags) either throws in time O(n) or returns, and it never allocates more than a fixed cap of pair keys — i.e. its running time is bounded by a function of the pairs it is allowed to emit, not by n^2 for an unvalidated n.

deferrals.theme: docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md's architecture snapshot still describes a two-tier (label-assignment default / core-aware fallback) constraint design that docs/findings/CONSTRAINT_FINDINGS.md decisively rejected before M1 shipped — the label-assignment tier (approach A) satisfied 0% of required-pair scenarios (triangles, matchings at n>=120) and was eliminated; only the core-aware tier (constrainedGreedy, approach B) was ported to lib/src/core.
deferrals.summary: No lib/src code issue — the core correctly implements only the single validated tier (buildConstrainedBuddyGraph -> constrainedGreedy -> optional polishConstrained), with no anonymous-graph-then-seat path anywhere in lib/src. This is filed only because a reader tracing 'the next committed change' through PROJECT_PLAN's section 3 would expect a label-assignment fast path in the core that does not exist and was deliberately dropped by research, not omitted by oversight.
deferrals.failure: A contributor reading PROJECT_PLAN.md section 3 before touching lib/src/core would look for (and might try to add) a label-assignment/seat-then-check tier that CONSTRAINT_FINDINGS.md already proved cannot carry hard required constraints.
deferrals.remediation: Update PROJECT_PLAN.md section 3 to point at CONSTRAINT_FINDINGS.md's conclusion (single core-aware tier), or note the two-tier text is superseded. This is a docs-accuracy fix, not a code change, and is filed as deferral because it has no caller/impact in lib/src today.
